name: CSS/JS Aggregation Retention
description: Prevents deletion of recent CSS/JS aggregates during cache rebuilds, improving performance on large sites.
project_description:
This module restores time-based garbage collection for CSS and JavaScript aggregates, preventing the complete deletion of aggregate directories during cache rebuilds that was introduced in Drupal 10.1.

Background

Drupal 10.1 introduced lazy generation of CSS/JS aggregate files. As part of that change, cache clearing was modified to delete the entire assets:// css and js directories during every cache rebuild (drush cr). While this works well for dynamic sites where aggregates regenerate on demand, it creates problems for statically generated sites and large sites that depend on previously aggregated files remaining on disk.

The module decorates core's CSS and JS collection optimizer services with subclasses that override deleteAll() to only remove files older than a configurable retention window (default 45 days), instead of deleting everything. It also ships two Drush commands for manual purging.

Related issue: https://www.drupal.org/node/3301716
